figures.finding: The Children's Act makes no exception for a child performer: the minimum age for employment is fifteen and for light work thirteen (work not harmful to health or development and not affecting school), no child may work at night (8 p.m. to 6 a.m.), and work in places of entertainment where a person may be exposed to immoral behaviour is hazardous, barred under eighteen; the rules reach any child's work, writing or directing included; no permit system exists in the Act.

value.hazardousIncludes: places of entertainment with exposure to immoral behaviour (under 18)

figures.applies: National (Act 560; later amendments, among them Act 937 of 2016, not read).

sources.said: Section 88. Prohibition of child labour at night. (1) No person shall engage a child in night work. (2) Night work constitutes work between the hours of eight o'clock in the evening and six o'clock in the morning.

Section 90. Minimum age for light work. The minimum age for the engagement of a child in light work shall be thirteen years. (2) Light work constitutes work which is not likely to be harmful to the health or development of the child and does not affect the child's attendance at school
(f) work in places such as bars, hotels and places of entertainment where a person may be exposed to immoral behaviour.

figures.finding: The National Film Authority's Film Development Fund lends (repayably) to filmmakers, producers, distributors and production companies who belong to a recognised industry body (the Actors Guild, the Producers Association, the Directors Guild ...) and are registered and tax-compliant with the Ghana Revenue Authority; no applicant age is stated.
figures.applies: National (as the press reports the NFA, 2026).

sources.said: For applicants, they must be a cinema theatre developer, filmmaker, producer, exhibitor, distributor or marketer, a television or film production company, and importantly must belong to a recognised professional group within the industry such as the Ghana Actors Guild,
1. It is not a “wonkye nni” fund. Beneficiaries are expected to repay funds received for their projects.
